sourceVerdicts.reasoning: Whole-formula C/H-only classification is taught and practised. No equation for every hydrocarbon is prescribed; this identity supplies composition vocabulary.

sourceVerdicts.sourceDemand: formula representation; not a new reaction family
sourceVerdicts.reasoning: Molecular/empirical/general/structural/displayed differences and a pent-2-ene transfer are explicit. Connected alcohol/acid/ester drawings supply the appropriate later Paper2C contexts. Condensed formula is explicitly not accepted as fully displayed.
Homologues, functional group and same-formula/different-connectivity isomers are explained and contrasted in practice. Definitions do not prescribe additional chemical interconversions.

Relevant first-six carbon roots, branch/alkene numbering and alcohol/acid/ester names are supported by practice. Later-family Paper2C limits are preserved; six-carbon naming does not mandate a new reaction for every compound or expand smaller drawing sets.

Both C4H10 connectivities and all three C5H12 skeletons have structural/displayed directions and original sheets; practice checks atoms/valency and duplicate rotations. This is structure deduction, not an isomerisation-reaction requirement.

Substitution, addition and combustion each have actual equations, structural change explanations and classification practice. UV and retained hydrogens distinguish halogen substitution from addition. Mechanisms are explicitly not required.
Crude oil composition is a mixture, with no single molecular formula or compulsory crude-oil reaction equation.
Fractionating-column teaching and practice distinguish physical separation from cracking, with temperature gradient/condensation and an original diagram. No new chemical equation is appropriate.
All six named fractions and uses are supplied and practised. Fractions remain mixtures, not six extra single-compound reaction requirements.
Colour, boiling range and viscosity trends and their temperature/mixture limitations are explained. Boiling does not break C–C bonds.

Fuel-energy lesson defines heat-releasing burning and separates ignition input from overall transfer. Existing combustion word/formula models support the context; it does not require an additional fuel species.

Complete combustion and both limiting incomplete CO/water and carbon/water models have word, balanced and condition-labelled state equations, with different-fuel practice. Hot water versus cooled liquid and real mixed products are explicit; no unique incomplete flame or mandatory particular fuel is invented.
CO oxygen-transport impairment is taught and distinguished from soot/CO2. No haemoglobin equation is required; haemoglobin references are explicitly optional.

Original organic lesson identifies high-temperature air nitrogen/oxygen; reconciliation supplies nitrogen + oxygen → nitrogen monoxide and N2(g)+O2(g)→2NO(g), plus practice and limitations. NO is representative of the required oxide family, not the entire exhaust or an imported detailed NOx mechanism.

Organic note explains sulfur-bearing impurities and explicitly uses S+O2→SO2 as a simple elemental-sulfur model. Existing inorganic combustion lesson supplies the matching word/state equation and S8 alternative when supplied. These shared references support1.25 without pretending every impurity is elemental S or every pure hydrocarbon contains sulfur.

sourceVerdicts.sourceDemand: explanatory chemical pathway, no unique exact sequence
sourceVerdicts.reasoning: Acid-rain lesson supplies the required SO2/NOx→atmospheric/water reactions→acidic rainwater explanation and transfer. Source does not prescribe a unique acid mixture or detailed atmospheric mechanism, so no missing universal balanced equation is inferred.

Cracking has general word products, one balanced hot-vapour feed/product model, silica/alumina and600–700°C, and atom-conservation transfer practice. C3H6 under the supplied acyclic one-C=C condition is correctly identified as propene; the example does not assert unique industrial products.
Cracking-demand teaching uses actual hypothetical supply/demand arithmetic and distinguishes molecular conversion from distillation. Reuses4.17 rather than prescribing extra feed/product equations.
CnH2n+2 and its acyclic-alkane restriction are taught; seven-carbon formula transfer does not impose naming/drawing or reaction demands beyond source scope.
Saturation is explained as molecular bonding, distinct from saturated solution. No separately prescribed chemical reaction.

Methane through pentane structural/displayed forms and all required small branched connectivities are supported by drawings and checking practice. Unbranched names and five-carbon drawing limit are retained; no equation for each drawing is required.

UV mono-substitution family has methane/chlorine word/state equation, methane/bromine illustration and ethane transfer. Organic product plus hydrogen halide, equivalent versus nonequivalent positions and further-substitution scope are explicit. No mechanism, all possible alkane–halogen combinations or invented phase is demanded.
C=C functional group is identified; actual bromine addition is assessed under4.27.
CnH2n restricted to the stated acyclic one-double-bond family is taught and practised; formula alone does not prove connectivity.
Unsaturation and ability to add are explained using C=C; no additional named reagent is prescribed here beyond the later addition family.

Ethene, propene, but-1-ene, but-2-ene and branched C4 alkene have structural/displayed support and practice; unbranched naming and no compulsory E/Z or cis/trans are retained. These are drawing demands, not new reaction cases.

Word products and structural bromine addition across C=C are given and checked using ethene plus propene/butene transfer. Skeleton/H atoms retained, one Br per original C=C carbon and no HBr. State-free connectivity plus expressly conditional nonaqueous state model avoids falsely treating bromine water as pure Br2(l) or guaranteeing a pure isolated product.

Bromine-water observation and alkane/alkene comparison are practised with no-UV, mixing, partitioning and excess-reagent limits. Reuses4.27 chemistry; the negative alkane test does not need a fictitious product equation.
Alcohol C–O–H group is distinguished from free OH− and carboxyl group. No additional conversion required.

All four required alcohols have structural and fully displayed sheets/practice: methanol, ethanol, propan-1-ol, butan-1-ol. Accepted short names and primary-only three/four-carbon limit retained. No requirement to oxidise every listed alcohol is inferred.

All three ethanol oxidation routes are separate: complete combustion, microbial oxygen-to-acid route, and heat with K2Cr2O7 in dilute H2SO4 to acid. Word/formula/conditional-state evidence exists; [O] is explicitly limited, and optional full molecular/ionic expansion separately balances actual species with12electrons. Route conditions/product endpoints remain distinct; no new mechanism/half-equation memorisation mandate.

Both named manufacture routes have word/balanced/state equations and correction/amount practice: steam hydration with phosphoric acid/about300°C/60–70atm; aqueous glucose fermentation with yeast enzymes/no air/about30°C. Hot ethanol gas versus later condensation, dissolved fermentation ethanol and ideal versus measured yield are explicit.
Air exclusion and enzyme optimum/denaturation are causally explained and practised, using existing glucose-fermentation model. No extra required aerobic-respiration reaction is created.
Full C(=O)–OH connectivity and carbonyl-carbon counting are explained and drawn in practice. No separate reaction.

Methanoic through butanoic acid structural/displayed forms, names, formulas and every oxygen/H connection are supported by original diagram and practice. Drawing set does not imply every possible acid/reagent combination.

Both prescribed aqueous-acid families have word/balanced/state equations: suitable metal→carboxylate+H2 and carbonate→carboxylate+CO2+water. Ethanoic/Mg and sodium-carbonate examples plus propanoic/Mg and calcium-carbonate practice preserve charge balance and soluble-product assumptions. No particular pairing is mislabelled mandatory; copper and gas-inference limits are explicit.
Vinegar is aqueous ethanoic-acid-containing mixture with concentration/inference limits. It does not add a new uniquely named reaction.
Ester C(=O)–O–C connectivity versus acid OH is supplied and practised. Functional-group demand is not an additional conversion.

The exact required ethanol+ethanoic-acid→ethyl-ethanoate+water case has word, balanced structural and conditional liquid-state equations, catalyst/reversibility explanation and transfer. [O] is rejected; both name fragments retained. No universal catalyst identity/temperature or pure isolated-product claim is added.

Ethyl ethanoate has an actual fully displayed diagram and construction/checking practice, including carbonyl, O–CH2 and all H. Molecular C4H8O2 alone is explicitly insufficient; linked formation equation supports but does not replace this drawing.

General ester formation/connectivity rule and both-direction practice identify alcohol/acid fragments, preserve carbonyl and display structures within six carbons. Examples include methyl pentanoate and propyl propanoate; reverse deduction is not falsely promoted to compulsory hydrolysis chemistry.
Volatility, distinctive smell and perfume/flavouring uses with inference limitations are taught. No chemical conversion or unique smell-identification equation is needed.

sourceVerdicts.sourceDemand: practical family with permitted named example
sourceVerdicts.reasoning: A supervised ester-preparation plan with ethanol/ethanoic acid, selected acid catalyst, controlled warming and method-dependent work-up is provided and practised. Exact formation equation is linked from4.39C. The source allows an ester such as ethyl ethanoate; alternative ester recipes are not an unfilled exhaustive list. Product purity/performed-practical claims are avoided.

Many monomers joining, C=C opening, atom retention, no removed small molecule and open-chain meaning are explained; new word/repeat models link all four required later examples. This is not misrepresented as a finite isolated molecule.

All four named repeats—poly(ethene), poly(propene), poly(chloroethene), poly(tetrafluoroethene)—have word models, correct open condensed repeats and the full displayed sheet; practice retains all substituents/outward bonds/n. State/industrial conditions are not fabricated for drawing requirements; no water removed.

Forward and reverse monomer/repeat deduction are taught and practised with chloroethene, tetrafluoroethene and propene, preserving branch/backbone identity. Typed open-repeat models supplement actual structure teaching. Reverse drawing is not a required depolymerisation experiment.

Persistence/nonbiodegradation and toxic combustion-product dependence are explained and practised: possible CO from incomplete burning and HCl from chlorine-containing polymer, without claiming all polymers contain chlorine. Source prescribes disposal explanation, not one exact universal incineration equation or detailed decomposition mechanism; shared CO limiting model supports the chemistry.

Diacid+diol→polyester+water family is explained via two functional ends and atom tracing; new word/ideal structural model distinguishes addition from condensation and identifies one water per link. No universal state/catalyst/temperature is prescribed.

sourceVerdicts.sourceDemand: named polyester repeat plus monomer-to-repeat method
sourceVerdicts.reasoning: Specifically required ethanedioic-acid/ethanediol pair has both monomer structures, a correct fully displayed polyester sheet, ideal structural equation and transfer/check practice. Both carbonyls and the ester link across the bracket boundary retained. C4H4O4 and2n-water ideal shorthand are distinguished from2n−1waters in one finite open chain; no phase invented.

Some biopolyesters biodegradable and condition-dependent interpretation are taught/practised. This does not prescribe an exact hydrolysis/degradation equation, all-polyester claim or universal degradation rate.

importantScopeFindings: 4.31C retains all three required routes; [O] alone is not counted as full actual reagent/state evidence. Optional full dichromate expansion now provides explicit molecular/ionic species and condition-labelled states without inventing extra syllabus memorisation.
4.32C retains both required manufacture routes and their different specified catalyst/air/temperature/pressure conditions; hot hydration gas and aqueous fermentation product states are conditional.
4.39C specifically requires ethyl ethanoate;4.43C allows an ester such as it. The chosen preparation reuses that chemistry and does not imply every alternative ester is a missing mandatory case.

4.27 structural bromine addition and4.28 bromine-water observation are related but distinct evidence. Conditional phases and aqueous-product limits are explicit; molecular counts alone do not prove connectivity or purity.

4.45 four open addition repeats and4.49C named polyester are present as typed structural models with full displayed-sheet links, not treated as finite closed molecules or forced into universal state labels.

No detailed acid-rain mechanism, complete polymer-incineration equation set, reverse-deduction hydrolysis procedure, depolymerisation reaction or full family Cartesian product is prescribed by these50 identities.
A missing direct model link is not automatically missing teaching:4.15 is supported by the original impurity explanation and shared sulfur combustion. This review records that cross-link explicitly.
